meta.name: visadb
meta.primary_source: English Wikipedia 'Visa requirements for X citizens' pages (per-corridor citations, day counts); corridors those pages don't cover fall back to passport-index
meta.limited_recognition: Abkhazia (AB), South Ossetia (OS), Transnistria (TS) and Northern Cyprus (NC) plus the SADR passport (EH, not a destination — no visa policy page exists) are hand-curated from Wikipedia stub pages in data/limited-recognition.json. A de facto passport is refused where it is not accepted as a travel document; accepted-but-undocumented regimes are marked assumed visa-required. Single-source: confidence=medium.
meta.visa_benefits: visa_holdings + visa_benefits (from data/visa-benefits.json) are a permit layer: 13 common foreign visa/residency holdings (US green card, US visa, Schengen visa/residence, UK BRP, Canada PR/visa, Australia PR, UAE residence, Japan visa, GCC residence, Singapore permit, APEC card) and the destinations each one unlocks. Curated from VisaCheck and verified against the destination's own Wikipedia row (a note in another country's row is that other country's policy, not the destination's — several VisaCheck entries were dropped or corrected on that basis). confidence=high means the destination's row documents it; medium means it fits the 'foreign visa/residence accepted' pattern but is not row-documented. A benefit only RELAXES the underlying passport rule (passport + admissibility still required); the app re-merges each against the passport result and keeps the better outcome. Each row carries source_page + source_url (the destination's 'Visa policy of X' Wikipedia page; Schengen states share 'Visa policy of the Schengen Area') for one-click re-verification.
meta.transit: Separate axis on visa_rules (transit, transit_note): free | required | conditional | unknown. Base rule — computed, not scraped — sets transit=free wherever the entry type is visa-free or freedom-of-movement (airside transit is strictly less privileged than entry) and unknown for every other corridor; cited exceptions live in data/transit.json and are applied by merge_transit(). Distinct from the entry ladder: a visa-free corridor is always transit-free, but a visa-required corridor may allow airside transit, require a transit visa, or be conditional on booked onward travel (China TWOV).
meta.mobility_regimes: Separate EXPLANATORY layer (mobility_regimes table, from data/mobility-regimes.json): the multilateral freedom-of-movement / free-movement blocs and which members currently exercise each right, so the app can explain WHY a corridor is visa-free / freedom-of-movement. It never changes the per-corridor visa_rules entry status. 'members' + 'associates' are active (a country counts as active in a regime if it is in either); 'deactivated' are bloc members that currently do NOT exercise the right (kept for reference, must not show). level: freedom-of-movement (enter + reside + work) or visa-free (enter without a visa, no automatic residence/work). Curated from the Wikipedia 'Freedom of movement' article.
meta.stay_rules: Separate FACTS layer (stay_rules table, from data/stay-rules.json): nationality-scoped stay allowances. The DB half of the stay-rules feature — it stores the facts, the app computes 'how many days do I have left' from these facts plus the user's own travel history (never stored). It never changes the per-corridor visa_rules entry status. window_type: per-entry (up to window_days each entry) or rolling (up to window_days in any window_period_days). zone: shared pool id — rows sharing a zone pool their allowance (Schengen: one 90/180 pool across 27 states; CA-4: one pool across GT/SV/HN/NI with per-country allowances), so 'time in one bloc country' is explicit. countries are real ISO2; nationalities may hold the sentinels '*' (all visa-exempt nationals) and 'EU-EEA' (EU/EEA nationals), resolved by the app. valid_from/valid_to bound when the grant applies. Phase-1 seed; re-verify per rule in phase 2.
meta.transit_benefits: Separate BENEFIT layer (transit_benefits table, from data/transit-benefits.json; T4): a foreign holding conferring transit (airside) rights at a hub, parallel to visa_benefits (which relaxes the ENTRY ladder). hub is a transit-regime id, not a country ('schengen' = airport-transit-visa regime; 'uk' = Direct Airside Transit regime); the app resolves a transit airport to a regime before querying. transit_type shares the visa_rules.transit vocabulary: 'free' = the holding waives the transit visa (airside), 'conditional' = waived only under the stated conditions (the visa-based Schengen exemptions require travel to/from the issuing country or the immediate return leg). Only VERIFIED benefits are stored, each with a source_url; a MISSING (holding, hub) row means 'no documented transit benefit from that holding at that hub' (the base corridor transit rule applies) — NOT a confirmed 'required'. Verified 2026-09-04 against the EU Visa Code + C(2024) 4319 Handbook + Germany AA + France-Visas, and gov.uk.
meta.stay_axis: Per-corridor stay axis on visa_rules (phase-2, auto-sourced from the same Wikipedia scrape; see also the curated stay_rules layer above for shared pools). window_period_days = Y when a cell states a rolling window ('90 days in 180') — NULL where Wikipedia omits it, which is the common case (it writes '90 days' and leaves 90/180 to convention), so most corridors have no stated period and the app should treat a bare day count as 'up to N days, window type unknown'. valid_to = the expiry date of THIS entry status (T6: a visa-free that lapses, e.g. a time-boxed agreement), kept only while it is still in the future relative to 'generated' — a lapsed 'until …' is a stale historical note, not a live expiry. Both are single-source (Wikipedia); cross-check before relying on a specific date. The app: if valid_to is set and the planned stay is after it, the grant has lapsed and the underlying visa status applies.

meta.disclaimer: General information, not legal advice. Rules change; always verify with the destination's official government source before booking.

AE.transit_note: Airside transit through the UAE requires no transit visa -- you may remain in the international transit area (all travellers are exempt from entry fees for the first 48 hours). A 96-hour transit visa is issued at the airport if you leave the transit area or your layover exceeds 48 hours (hotel booking required for some nationalities). Nationals of Iran are refused entry and transit (2026).

AU.transit_note: Transit visa (subclass 771) required to transit airside through Australia unless you are on the transit-without-visa list or you depart by air within 8 hours of arrival with a confirmed onward booking and remain in the transit lounge. CA.transit_note: A transit visa is required to transit through Canada when you need a visa or eTA to enter. GB.transit_note: Direct Airside Transit visa (DATV) required to transit airside through the UK -- airside transit is available only at London Heathrow and Manchester -- when you need a visa to enter and are not on the exempt list.

IN.transit_note: India requires a transit visa (15 days, single or double entry, onward ticket needed) or a transit e-Visa (30 days) to transit through the country; apply before travel. Some short airside connections may be exempt -- verify with your airline or the Bureau of Immigration.

JP.transit_note: Airside transit through Japan requires no visa while you remain in the transit area. KR.transit_note: Airside transit through South Korea requires no visa for less than 24 hours at Incheon (or the same calendar day at other airports), as long as you stay within the transit area. NZ.transit_note: A Transit Visa is required to transit through New Zealand (airside, Auckland Airport only, up to 24 hours) when you are not a visa-waiver national and are not on the transit visa waiver list.

Organised tour groups (all nationalities except Georgia) may stay up to 24 hours with a free electronic authorisation. Entry via Russia: Russian visa rules also apply. Abkhaz stamps may lead to fines or entry refusal in Georgia.

AE.transit_note: Airside transit through the UAE requires no transit visa -- you may remain in the international transit area (all travellers are exempt from entry fees for the first 48 hours). A 96-hour transit visa is issued at the airport if you leave the transit area or your layover exceeds 48 hours (hotel booking required for some nationalities). Nationals of Iran are refused entry and transit (2026).

AT.transit_note: Airport transit visa (ATV) required to transit airside through any Schengen airport (or Cyprus), even without leaving the international transit area (EU common list, Visa Code Reg. 810/2009). Not required if you hold a valid EU/EEA/CA/JP/US visa or residence permit.

AU.transit_note: Transit visa (subclass 771) required to transit airside through Australia unless you are on the transit-without-visa list or you depart by air within 8 hours of arrival with a confirmed onward booking and remain in the transit lounge. A Transit visa is always required for Gold Coast airport, and for Cairns and Sydney if staying overnight.

Trudeau, or Montreal for CTP), and leave within 24 hours staying in the sterile international transit area.

CN.transit_note: 24-hour transit without visa (TWOV): transit through mainland China without a visa for up to 24 hours -- arrive by air, cruise ship or rail with a confirmed (not standby) onward ticket to a third country departing within 24 hours; passport valid 3+ months. Available to most nationalities at most ports, especially for airside connections.

GB.transit_note: Direct Airside Transit visa (DATV) required to transit airside through the UK -- airside transit is available only at London Heathrow and Manchester -- when you need a visa to enter and are not on the exempt list.

IN.transit_note: India requires a transit visa (15 days, single or double entry, onward ticket needed) or a transit e-Visa (30 days) to transit through the country; apply before travel. Some short airside connections may be exempt -- verify with your airline or the Bureau of Immigration.

KR.transit_note: Airside transit through South Korea requires no visa for less than 24 hours at Incheon (or the same calendar day at other airports), as long as you stay within the transit area. Non-visa-exempt nationals may also qualify for a 30-day transit visa exemption if they hold a visa or residence permit from Australia, Canada and other listed states and meet the routing rules.

NC.note: free visa on arrival at designated ports and border crossings, 90 days within any 180-day period. Citizens of the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland and Türkiye may enter with an ID card instead of a passport. Stays beyond 90 days require a residence permit.

NZ.transit_note: A Transit Visa is required to transit through New Zealand (airside, Auckland Airport only, up to 24 hours) when you are not a visa-waiver national and are not on the transit visa waiver list.

OS.note: no visas issued; entry permit required — invitation from a party in South Ossetia, processed by the Immigration Control Office of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (up to 30 calendar days). Entry only via Russia: a Russian visa or exemption is required. Register within 3 days of arrival.

QA.transit_note: Airside transit through Hamad International Airport requires no transit visa regardless of nationality if you depart within 24 hours. Qatar Airways passengers with layovers of 5 to 96 hours can obtain a free transit visa to leave the airport.

TS.note: no visa required — 45-day migration card on entry, extendable up to 3 years; internal passport or ID card accepted. Entry is land-only via Moldova or Ukraine — that country's entry requirements also apply.

US.transit_note: C-1 transit visa required to transit through the United States (immediate and continuous transit en route to another country) when you need a visa to enter. VWP (visa-free) nationals do not need a C-1 -- they use ESTA.

AB.note: entry permit required (Abkhazia MFA). Children aged 14 and under enter visa-free regardless of nationality. Organised tour groups (all nationalities except Georgia) may stay up to 24 hours with a free electronic authorisation. Entry via Russia: Russian visa rules also apply. Abkhaz stamps may lead to fines or entry refusal in Georgia.

AU.transit_note: No Transit visa (771) is needed (you are visa-exempt). AE.transit_note: Airside transit through the UAE requires no transit visa -- you may remain in the international transit area (all travellers are exempt from entry fees for the first 48 hours). Nationals of Iran are refused entry and transit (2026).

AU.transit_note: Transit visa (subclass 771) required to transit airside through Australia unless you are on the transit-without-visa list or you depart by air within 8 hours of arrival with a confirmed onward booking and remain in the transit lounge. CN.transit_note: 24-hour transit without visa (TWOV): transit through mainland China without a visa for up to 24 hours -- arrive by air, cruise ship or rail with a confirmed (not standby) onward ticket to a third country departing within 24 hours; passport valid 3+ months. IN.transit_note: India requires a transit visa (15 days, single or double entry, onward ticket needed) or a transit e-Visa (30 days) to transit through the country; apply before travel. Some short airside connections may be exempt -- verify with your airline or the Bureau of Immigration.

KR.transit_note: Airside transit through South Korea requires no visa for less than 24 hours at Incheon (or the same calendar day at other airports), as long as you stay within the transit area. JP.transit_note: Airside transit through Japan requires no visa while you remain in the transit area. AB.note: entry permit required (Abkhazia MFA). Children aged 14 and under enter visa-free regardless of nationality. Organised tour groups (all nationalities except Georgia) may stay up to 24 hours with a free electronic authorisation. Entry via Russia: Russian visa rules also apply. Abkhaz stamps may lead to fines or entry refusal in Georgia.

AE.transit_note: Airside transit through the UAE requires no transit visa -- you may remain in the international transit area (all travellers are exempt from entry fees for the first 48 hours). A 96-hour transit visa is issued at the airport if you leave the transit area or your layover exceeds 48 hours (hotel booking required for some nationalities). Nationals of Iran are refused entry and transit (2026).

AU.transit_note: Transit visa (subclass 771) required to transit airside through Australia unless you are on the transit-without-visa list or you depart by air within 8 hours of arrival with a confirmed onward booking and remain in the transit lounge. A Transit visa is always required for Gold Coast airport, and for Cairns and Sydney if staying overnight.

CA.transit_note: No transit visa is needed (you are visa-exempt). An eTA is required only if you leave the international transit area; a strictly airside connection -- same or separate ticket -- needs no authorization as long as you do not clear immigration.

CN.transit_note: 24-hour transit without visa (TWOV): transit through mainland China without a visa for up to 24 hours -- arrive by air, cruise ship or rail with a confirmed (not standby) onward ticket to a third country departing within 24 hours; passport valid 3+ months. Available to most nationalities at most ports, especially for airside connections.

GB.transit_note: Direct Airside Transit visa (DATV) required to transit airside through the UK -- airside transit is available only at London Heathrow and Manchester -- when you need a visa to enter and are not on the exempt list.

IN.transit_note: India requires a transit visa (15 days, single or double entry, onward ticket needed) or a transit e-Visa (30 days) to transit through the country; apply before travel. Some short airside connections may be exempt -- verify with your airline or the Bureau of Immigration.

JP.transit_note: Airside transit through Japan requires no visa while you remain in the transit area. The 72-hour transit-without-visa (TWOV) additionally allows entry for up to 72 hours (sightseeing, rest) when you are transiting to a third country and obtain a transit or shore pass from the carrier.

KR.transit_note: Airside transit through South Korea requires no visa for less than 24 hours at Incheon (or the same calendar day at other airports), as long as you stay within the transit area. Non-visa-exempt nationals may also qualify for a 30-day transit visa exemption if they hold a visa or residence permit from Australia, Canada and other listed states and meet the routing rules.

NC.note: free visa on arrival at designated ports and border crossings, 90 days within any 180-day period. Citizens of the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland and Türkiye may enter with an ID card instead of a passport. Stays beyond 90 days require a residence permit.

NZ.transit_note: A Transit Visa is required to transit through New Zealand (airside, Auckland Airport only, up to 24 hours) when you are not a visa-waiver national and are not on the transit visa waiver list.

corrections.note: Argentine citizens: 90-day visa-free stay in Russia (within any 180-day period), but since 2025-06-30 a pre-travel ETA is mandatory - pre-register in the Gosuslugi RuID app and obtain a digital code at least 72 hours before entry. Sources: Timatic AR->RU; gosuslugi.ru; ruID app; Wikipedia 'Visa requirements for Argentine citizens'.

Argentine citizens need a Vietnam eVisa for 90 days for general entry; the visa-free 30-day option applies to Phu Quoc Island only. Sources: Timatic AR->VN; Vietnam eVisa (evisa.gov.vn); Wikipedia 'Visa requirements for Argentine citizens'.

British citizens get a 30-day visa-free stay in Belarus (dataset previously said 10). The waiver is time-limited: valid until 2026-12-31. Note: UK FCDO advises against travel to Belarus on safety grounds. Sources: Timatic GB->BY; UK gov.uk 'Belarus: entry requirements'; Wikipedia 'Visa requirements for British citizens'.

British citizens need a visa for Iran (stamped in the passport before arrival) - NOT visa-free. The 2026-09-04 build mis-scraped this: Wikipedia's 'Visa requirements for British citizens' lists Kish Island (a visa-free Iranian island) as a sub-row reusing the Iran flag, and the parser let that exception overwrite Iran's main 'Visa required' status (parser now fixed: the main row wins). Timatic GB->IR and passport-index both say visa-required. Sources: Wikipedia 'Visa requirements for British citizens' (Iran row + Timatic GB->IR); passportindex.org.
Thailand reverted its 2024 visa-exemption expansion on 2026-05-19; Morocco dropped from the exempt lists, e-visa required from 2026-06-07. Sources: Thai MFA lists; Royal Thai Embassy Rabat advisory.
Brazil reciprocal e-visa for Mexican nationals, effective 2026-02-05 (mirrors the BR e-visa already required from US/CA/AU). Sources: Wikipedia 'Visa policy of Brazil'; Fragomen 2026 advisory.

Russian citizens need an Australian visitor visa (subclass 600), applied online via ImmiAccount - not visa-free. Sources: Timatic RU->AU; Australian Department of Home Affairs 'Visitor (subclass 600)'; Wikipedia 'Visa requirements for Russian citizens'.
Russian citizens get up to 90 days visa-free in Costa Rica (dataset previously said 30). Sources: Timatic RU->CR; Wikipedia 'Visa requirements for Russian citizens'.
Russian citizens get up to 183 days visa-free in Peru (dataset previously said 90). Sources: Timatic RU->PE; Wikipedia 'Visa requirements for Russian citizens'.

mobility_regimes.name: Central America-4
mobility_regimes.note: The CA-4 Border Control Agreement (2006) abolished land border checks among El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua, with a harmonised external border (open-border for land travel; kept as visa-free).

mobility_regimes.name: Caribbean Community (CARICOM)
mobility_regimes.note: Full free movement (live + work, no time limits) is implemented among Barbados, Belize, Dominica and St Vincent and the Grenadines since 1 Oct 2025. The other CARICOM members are visa-free only and are marked deactivated so they do not show.

mobility_regimes.name: Commonwealth of Independent States
mobility_regimes.note: CIS mobility agreements: visa-free travel, document recognition and labour cooperation among members - a common market, shallower than the EAEU single market, so no full freedom of movement. Ukraine's participation is suspended; Turkmenistan is an associate member.

mobility_regimes.name: Compact of Free Association
mobility_regimes.note: Citizens of the Federated States of Micronesia, the Marshall Islands and Palau may enter, reside, study and work in the United States indefinitely without a visa.

mobility_regimes.name: Common Travel Area
mobility_regimes.note: The UK, Ireland and the Crown Dependencies (Isle of Man, Jersey, Guernsey - not in VisaDB) share a Common Travel Area with no routine border controls on people.

mobility_regimes.name: Eurasian Economic Union
mobility_regimes.note: Single market: free movement of labour without work permits since 2012; a national ID/internal passport is valid within the union. The deeper 5-state core inside the CIS.

mobility_regimes.name: European Union / EEA / EFTA
mobility_regimes.note: EU internal free movement (enter, reside, work, study). Extended to Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway via the EEA, and to Switzerland (EFTA) via the EU-Switzerland Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons. The Nordic Passport Union (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden) is subsumed here; its extra territories - the Faroe Islands (an NPU member) and Greenland (open border with the Nordics) - are not tracked in VisaDB.

mobility_regimes.name: Gulf Cooperation Council
mobility_regimes.note: GCC citizens may live, work and reside freely in the other GCC states.

mobility_regimes.name: India-Bhutan
mobility_regimes.note: Indian and Bhutanese citizens may cross the border with no passport (a long-standing open-border arrangement); kept as visa-free.

mobility_regimes.name: India-Nepal open border
mobility_regimes.note: Under the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, Indian and Nepali citizens may live, work, own property and trade in each other's country; the border is open.

mobility_regimes.name: Mercosur
mobility_regimes.note: No passport required to travel between members; freedom of movement also extends to associate states (Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru). Venezuela is suspended.

mobility_regimes.name: Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS)
mobility_regimes.note: OECS citizens may enter, reside, study and work in each member state indefinitely without a visa.

mobility_regimes.name: Schengen Area
mobility_regimes.note: Schengen Area short-stay travel zone: 28 states with abolished internal border controls - the EU member states in Schengen plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland (EFTA), Romania and Bulgaria. A valid Schengen short-stay visa or a Schengen/EU residence permit grants 90-in-180-day visa-free travel across these states. Level is 'visa-free' (short-stay entry), NOT freedom-of-movement (no automatic right to reside/work). Excludes EU-but-non-Schengen Ireland and Cyprus. Bulgaria is included per the current product definition of the Schengen travel area; verify its border-control status for a specific travel date.

mobility_regimes.name: Trans-Tasman Travel Arrangement
mobility_regimes.note: Australian and New Zealand citizens may live, work and study in each other's country (reciprocal resident-class rights), beyond simple visa-free entry.

mobility_regimes.name: Union State of Russia and Belarus
mobility_regimes.note: Deepest integration: equal rights to freedom of movement and choice of place of residence between Russia and Belarus.

transit_benefits.note: A valid Canadian permanent resident card guarantees unconditional readmission, so no Schengen airport transit visa is needed for airside transit. Airside only.

A valid Canadian visa exempts from the Schengen airport transit visa, but only when travelling to/from Canada (or to another third country, or returning from Canada immediately after using the visa). Airside only.

A valid Japanese visa exempts from the Schengen airport transit visa, but only when travelling to/from Japan (or to another third country, or returning from Japan immediately after using the visa). Airside only.
A valid residence permit issued by a Schengen/EU Member State — no airport transit visa needed.
A valid Schengen (uniform) visa, national long-stay visa, or residence permit issued by a Member State — no airport transit visa needed (full Schengen access includes transit).

DISCREPANCY: a valid UK residence permit (BRP/ILR) is listed as a Schengen airport-transit-visa exemption in the 2024 EU Visa Code Handbook (point (c)) and French practice (must guarantee unconditional readmission), but is NOT listed in the 2019 Visa Code Annex V or Germany's FAQ. Applies to the residence permit only — NOT a UK visitor visa. Airside only. Verify with the specific transit state before travel.

A valid UK Standard Visitor visa is explicitly listed on gov.uk as exempt from the UK Direct Airside Transit visa (DATV). Airside only. A UK residence permit (BRP/ILR) holder has leave to remain and can enter the UK, so a DATV is not the applicable route. Note: the status of most OTHER foreign holdings for the DATV is currently UNVERIFIED (the UK rules were restructured and the relevant appendix is unpublished), so no rows are written for them.

A valid US permanent resident card (green card / I-551) guarantees unconditional readmission, so no Schengen airport transit visa is needed for airside transit. Airside only — leaving the international transit area needs a Schengen short-stay visa.

A valid US visa exempts from the Schengen airport transit visa, but only when travelling to/from the US (or to another third country, or returning from the US immediately after using the visa). Airside only.
